# `{qnp}`

<!-- badges: start -->

```{r, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, results='asis'}
library(badger)
cat(
  badge_lifecycle(stage = "experimental", alt = "Lifecycle: experimental"),
```

<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of `{qnp}` ("quarto-notes plots") is to provide helpers for including plots in Quarto notes.
It currently provides one function,
`interactive_plot()`,
which makes a `{ggplot2}` plot interactive in HTML output
and leaves it unchanged in other output formats.

## Installation

You can install the development version of `{qnp}` from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("Morrison-Lab/qnp")
```

## Example

`interactive_plot()` takes a `ggplot`
and a text alternative (`alt`) for the plot:

```{r example, fig.alt = "Scatterplot of fuel economy (miles per gallon) versus car weight"}
library(ggplot2)
library(qnp)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point()

interactive_plot(
  plot = p,
  alt = "Scatterplot of fuel economy versus car weight",
  is_html = FALSE
)
```

In HTML output
(the default, via `is_html = knitr::is_html_output()`),
the result is an interactive [plotly](https://plotly.com/r/) widget
wrapped in a `<div>` with `role = "img"` and `aria-label = alt`,
so that screen readers announce it as a single image.
In other output formats,
the original `ggplot` is returned unchanged.
This README is rendered to GitHub-flavored Markdown,
which knitr counts as an HTML output format,
so the example sets `is_html = FALSE` explicitly
to show the static plot.

See [USAGE.md](USAGE.md) for more details.

## Development

### Building the Documentation Site

This package uses [altdoc](https://altdoc.etiennebacher.com/) with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) to build its documentation site. To build and preview the documentation locally:

```r
# Load the package
pkgload::load_all()

# Render the documentation
altdoc::render_docs()

# Preview the site
altdoc::preview_docs()
```

The documentation is automatically built and deployed to GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions when changes are pushed to the main branch.
